preconditions.description: The number of employees n and events m are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= t <= 3 for t in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin_lines[1:]])
preconditions.description: Every event type t is an integer between 1 and 3 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n for line in stdin_lines[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 1)
preconditions.description: For type 1 events, employee IDs x and y are valid within the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n for line in stdin_lines[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 2)
preconditions.description: For type 2 events, the employee ID x is valid within the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= i <= current_packet_count for line in stdin_lines[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 3)
preconditions.description: For type 3 events, x is a valid employee and i is a valid index of a previously issued packet.
It is guaranteed that when a type 1 event occurs, employee x does not currently have a boss, and the company structure remains acyclic.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout_lines) == len([line for line in stdin_lines[1:] if int(line.split()[0]) == 3])
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of type 3 queries in the input.

postconditions.expression: all(line in ['YES', 'NO'] for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is exactly 'YES' or 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: all((line == 'YES') == (is_ancestor_in_tree_at_time(query_time, x, root_of_packet[i-1])) for line, (x, i, query_time) in zip(stdout_lines, query_data))
postconditions.description: For each query (x, i) at time t, the output is 'YES' if and only if x is an ancestor of the employee who received packet i in the hierarchy existing at time t, where i is 1-based index of packets and query_time is the chronological index of the query event.
